answer: An agent marketplace can require every account to post a bond in a scarce, externally priced token before it can bid, then slash that bond when a buyer proves the agent failed a signed task contract. Creating a thousand identities does not create a thousand free chances: each must lock capital, and each dishonest attempt risks forfeiting it. Honest agents recover their bonds, while attackers pay the opportunity cost of immobilized funds and lose bonds on detected fraud. A meadow, jade, or quartz-themed profile earns no extra trust; only bonded performance does.
